<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />preferable], in both places as perfect frequentative; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=5}} referring to the future, unless with Stade, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} vi. 189, we read {{GHGheb|text=וְהַצֵּיל}} and {{GHGheb|text=וְהַמְלֵיט}}), or an imperfect consecutive ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=13}}) or participle ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=5}}); cf. also ''u''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|u}}
2. The idea of long ''continuance'' is very frequently expressed by the verb {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to go}}, along with its infinitive absolute, or even by the latter alone, and this occurs not only when it can be taken in its literal sense (''to go, to walk'', as in the examples given above, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=9}}, 13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=19|hidebook=1}}; cf. also, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}}, where both infinitives stand ''before'' the verb, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=126|verse=6}}, where {{GHGheb|text=הָלוֹךְ}} precedes), but in cases where {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}} in the sense of ''to go on, to continue'', merely performs also the function of an adverb. The action itself is added in a second infinitive absolute, or sometimes (see above, ''t'') in a participle or verbal adjective. Examples, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּשֻׁ֫בוּ הַמַּ֫יִם... הָלוֹךְ וָשׁוֹב|translate=and the waters returned... continually}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=11}}; with a participle following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=16}} (unless we read {{GHGheb|text=וּבָכֹה}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=16}}); with an adjective following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=10}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=9}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=25}}.<ref>Cf. in French, ''Le mal va toujours croissant, la maladie va toujours en augmentant et en empirant'', ‘''continually increases and becomes worse and worse''.’</ref>

On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=41}} the participle {{GHGheb|text=הֹלֵךְ}} is used instead of the infinitive absolute. Of a different kind are the instances in which the participle {{GHGheb|text=הֹלֵךְ}} is used as predicate along with the co-ordinate adjective ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=17|verse=12}}) or participle ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=6}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|v}}
3. The regular place of the negative is between the intensifying infinitive absolute and the finite verb,<ref>Cf. Rieder, ''Quo loco ponantur negationes'' {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} ''et'' {{GHGheb|text=אַל}}... (''Zeitschrift für Gymn.-Wesen'', 1879, p. 395 ff.).</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהַצֵּל לֹֽא־הִצַּלְתָּ|translate=neither hast thou delivered at all}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=11|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=10}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַל}}). Exceptions are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=4}} (where the negation of the threat pronounced in 2:17 is expressed in the same form of words); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|w}}
4. With a finite verb of one of the derived conjugations, not only the infinitive absolute of the ''same'' conjugation may be connected ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=22}} Piʿēl; 17:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=3}} Niphʿal; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=15}} Puʿal; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=18}} Hiphʿîl; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}} Hophʿal), but also (especially with Niphʿal, rarely with Piʿēl and Hiphʿîl; see Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=18}}) that of {{GHGterm|Qal}} as the simplest and most general representative of the verbal idea, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=18}} (with Piʿēl; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=28|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=טֹרַף}} is a passive of Qal, {{GHGpar|52|e}}); 46:4 (with Hiphʿîl); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=2}} (with Niphʿal); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=19}} (with Hithpoʿēl; {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫עָה}} in the same verse must also, according to the Masora, certainly be the infinitive absolute Qal; see {{GHGpar|67|o}}), and so always {{GHGheb|text=מוֹת יוּמַת|translate=he shall surely be put to death}}. Elsewhere the infinitive absolute of a conjugation with kindred meaning is found, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=23}} Hophʿal for Niphʿal (but most probably we should read, with Driver, the ''infin. Niph.'' in both places, {{GHGheb|text=הִפָּדֵה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽחָרֵב}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=16}} (Piʿēl for Hiphʿîl, unless {{GHGheb|text=יְקַטְּרוּן}} is to be read); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}} (Hophʿal for Puʿal).<ref>In three passages even the infinitive absolute of another stem of like sound occurs; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=אָדוֹשׁ}} is no doubt a mere textual error for {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹשׁ}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=13}}, according to {{GHGpar|72|aa}}, we should read {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסְפֵם}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹסֵף}}. Barth, ''Nom.-bildung'', § 49 ''b'', sees in {{GHGheb|text=אָדוֹשׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=אָסוֹף}} infinitives {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, exactly corresponding in form to ''ʾ<sup>a</sup>qâm''[ā] the Aram. infin. ʾAphʿēl of {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}; but there is no more evidence for a ''Hiph.'' of {{GHGheb|text=דּוּשׁ}} in Hebrew than for a stem {{GHGheb|text=אָדַשׁ}}.</ref> Finally, the infinitive absolute may<section end=par113 /><noinclude>
